pimarane-type diterpenes are promising as a class to develop new effective anticariogen agents.

seven pimarane-type diterpenes were evaluated in vitro for their antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and two semi-synthesis pimarane derivatives, PA and PA-NA, showed to be the most active compounds.
the antimicrobial activity of seven pimarane-type diterpenes against oral pathogens responsible for dental carious disease is reported for the first time.

the discovery of new compounds from Viguiera species with potential application in oral care products.

the discovery and evaluation of new natural antimicrobial agents against microorganisms responsible for oral diseases, and the results obtained are a valuable contribution to the discovery of novel antimicrobial agents.

the search and development of new compounds with potential application in the oral health field, and the discovery of new antimicrobial compounds that can be employed as a class of novel effective anticariogenic agent is a major goal of our research group.

the diterpenes from Viguiera are a promising source of new antimicrobial agents.
the pimarane type diterpenes, especially the ent-15-pimarane-8b, 19-diol, ent-pimara 8(14), 15-dien-3β-ol and ent-pimara8(14),19-dien-3-ol are potential candidates for use in dental care products.
these pimaranes have potential for the development of novel anticariogenic agents.

the antimicrobial activity of the diterpene compounds is mainly related to the hydrophobicity of the molecule.
pimarane type diterpenes are a promising group of compounds for the development of oral health care products.
the pimarane-type diterpenes are promising candidates for the development of novel anticariogenic drugs.

the pimarane type diterpenes isolated from Viguiera species are a promising class of compounds with potential as new anticariogenic agents.
